## In Silico Mutagenesis
Returns feature predictions from a finished run of in silico mutagenesis.
### URL parameters
- `sequence_name`: String name of the submitted sequence.
- `feature_name`: String name of the desired feature value.
- `feature_only`: If set, does not return position, ref, or alt columns.

**Note:** the examples below depend on the in silico mutagenesis example from POST having completed successfully. You must use the `job_id` from the POST response.

post.description:
Submit a gene list for community detection and poll for the result.

**Asynchronous flow:**

1. First POST with `entrez` body and `body_tag` query param: the Celery task is submitted and the endpoint returns `202 Accepted` with `{"status": "processing"}` immediately. The client must then poll.
2. Subsequent POSTs with the same `body_tag` (empty body): return `202` while the task is still running, or `200` with the full result once the task has completed and cached the payload in Redis.
3. Cached results are served on repeat polls, so refreshing returns immediately.

**`body_tag` is required** for any request that submits a new gene list — it is the key used for polling and caching.

parameters.name: body_tag
parameters.description: Required. Stable identifier used to key the in-flight task and the cached result in Redis. Clients must send the same value on the initial submission and every subsequent poll.

parameters.name: comembership
parameters.description: Return / partition only the edges with comembership scores above the specified membership percentage (default 90 percent)

parameters.name: extended_universe
parameters.description: When true, includes all organism annotations in the enrichment background population, matching the behavior of previous API versions. Default restricts the background to human-annotated genes for the hypergeometric test.

parameters.name: false_dscv_rate
parameters.description: Sets the minimum Q value for Benjamini-Hochberg p-value correction of multiple hypothesis test.

parameters.name: giant_version
parameters.description: Version of GIANT to use. Defaults to v1.

parameters.name: integration
parameters.description: Integration used to make a new request.

parameters.name: iterations
parameters.description: The number of partitions to predict (default 10)

parameters.name: neighbour_count
parameters.description: For each submitted gene, the maximum number of neighbours to count starting with top weighted (default 50)

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Optional user generated title for the query.

parameters.name: top_sknn
parameters.description: Filter for the top % of edges in sknn (default 5 percent)

200.description: Community detection result. Returned on polls after the Celery task has finished.

202.description: Task submitted or still running. Body is `{"status": "processing"}`. Poll the same endpoint with the same `body_tag` (empty body) until `200` is returned.

400.description: Missing `body_tag`, invalid `giant_version`, unknown integration, gene list shorter than MIN_QUERY_SIZE, or polled a `body_tag` that has no cached result and no in-flight task.

post.description:
Submit a gene-level GWAS file as multipart/form-data. Choose v1 for NetWAS on GIANT networks or v3 for MAGE-WAS on MAGE networks. The default is v1.

A successful submission returns 201 with the saved job, including its UUID. Poll GET /api/netwas/{id}/ to track status and obtain the results_file URL when completed. The title and email fields are optional. Request examples show a filename for gwas_file; send the actual file bytes in that multipart field.
post.summary: Create a NetWAS or MAGE-WAS job

gwas_file.description:
Gene-level GWAS file. Three formats are auto-detected:

**VEGAS / VEGAS2** (8 or more whitespace-separated columns): `Chr Gene nSNPs nSims Start Stop TestStat Pvalue [...]` - gene identifier in column 2, p-value in column 8.

**MAGMA .genes.out** (9 columns): `GENE CHR START STOP NSNPS NPARAM N ZSTAT P` - gene identifier in column 1, p-value in column 9.

**Plain 2-column**: `GENE<TAB>P_VALUE` - gene identifier in column 1, p-value in column 2.

For VEGAS and MAGMA, only the gene and p-value columns are used; the remaining columns are read but ignored.

A header row is optional in all formats and is auto-detected. Lines beginning with `#` are skipped (MAGMA-style comments). Gene identifiers may be HGNC standard symbols or Entrez IDs. File must be < 3 MB with a .txt / .csv / .tsv / .out extension.

v1 example files (the same BMI GWAS in each format): [VEGAS](https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/humanbase/netwas/examples/bmi-vegas.txt), [MAGMA](https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/humanbase/netwas/examples/bmi-magma.genes.out), [2-column](https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/humanbase/netwas/examples/bmi-2column.tsv).

v3 example files (MAGE-WAS Alzheimer's demonstration subset, 1,008 genes; for trying v3, not for results): [VEGAS](https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/humanbase/netwas/examples/alzheimer-vegas.txt), [MAGMA](https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/humanbase/netwas/examples/alzheimer-magma.genes.out), [2-column](https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/humanbase/netwas/examples/alzheimer-2column.tsv).

Collected defects are returned together in the gwas_file error list.

tissue.description: The tissue network: an Integration slug for the chosen version, as listed by /api/integrations/ (for example brain for v1, brain-v3 for v3).

p_value.description: Required for v1: p-value cutoff for SVM training. Genes below the cutoff are positives; genes at or above it are negatives. Ignored for v3, which uses the uploaded gene p-values directly and stores this field as null.

mhc.description: Used by v3 only; ignored for v1 (stored as null). Whether MAGE-WAS trains on the chr6 MHC region. Its long-range linkage makes one signal light up a whole block, so exclude is the default. Use keep for autoimmune traits, where the region carries the real signal.

version.description: Network version: v1 runs NetWAS on GIANT networks; v3 runs MAGE-WAS on MAGE networks.

value.title: BMI on the GIANT brain network
Alzheimer's disease on the MAGE brain network

400.description: Invalid input. Field names map to lists of error messages, including tissue, p_value, and mhc. Upload errors use a gwas_file list containing all collected defects, or the first line of a rejection message. Upload errors for v1 also return stats (mapping counts against the p-value cutoff, or null); v3 has no cutoff, so its upload errors return only gwas_file.

429.description: The submitting IP already has 5 queued or running jobs, across v1 and v3. Wait for a job to finish before submitting again.

get.description: Retrieve a NetWAS (v1, GIANT) or MAGE-WAS (v3, MAGE) job by the UUID returned at submission. Poll status for progress; completed jobs provide results_file and log_file URLs. The mhc field is null for v1; p_value is null for v3.

200.description: NetWAS job retrieved successfully.

404.description: No job exists with this id.

post.description:
## SEEK Create
Creates a SEEK result using the provided input parameters in the request body.
### Request Body
*This endpoint accepts a POST request with a JSON payload:*

- `body_tag`: A string representing the body tag.
- `query_genes`: A list of dictionaries representing genes.
- `term_list`: A list of term dictionaries containing 'label' and 'value' keys.
- `query_organism`: A string representing the slug for the query organism.

200.description: Returns SEEK results

post.description:
## SEEK Enrichment
Retrieves gene enrichment data for the provided query genes.
### Request Body
*This endpoint accepts a POST request with a JSON payload:*

- `body_tag`: A string representing the body tag.
- `query_genes`: A list of dictionaries representing genes.
- `term_list`: A list of term dictionaries containing 'label' and 'value' keys.
- `query_organism`: A string representing the slug for the query organism.

200.description: Returns SEEK enrichment results

post.description:
## SEEK Expression
Retrieves gene expression data for the provided query genes and datasets.
### Request Body
*This endpoint accepts a POST request with a JSON payload:*

- `body_tag`: A string representing the body tag.
- `datasets`: **_(optional)_** An optional list of strings representing dataset IDs.
- `page`: **_(optional)_** The requested page number for pagination. Defaults to 1.
- `page_y`: **_(optional)_** The requested page number for pagination on the Y-axis. Defaults to 1.
- `reference_organism`: A string representing the slug for the reference organism.
- `filter_entrez`: **_(optional)_** An optional list of integers representing the Entrez IDs to filter.
- `query_genes`: A list of dictionaries representing genes.
- `term_list`: A list of term dictionaries containing 'label' and 'value' keys.
- `query_organism`: A string representing the slug for the query organism.

200.description: Returns SEEK expression results

GeneDetail.description:
A single gene, plus which compendiums contain it.

Separate from GeneSerializer because that one also renders network nodes,
variant genes and term annotations, which are list payloads that neither
need availability nor should pay to compute it.

Always emits a list. `[]` means the gene is in the catalog but in no
compendium; the field being absent would instead mean availability is
unknown, and clients treat those differently.
